title: Self-Regulating Acoustic Feedback Resonator with Dynamic Hysteresis Limiting (Series A)
assignee: Zazie Institute of Applied Anomalies / Zazie Productions LLC
abstract: A speculative electroacoustic system and method for generating sustained polyphonic acoustic resonance in enclosed architectural spaces without runaway acoustic distortion, utilizing analog optical gain limiters and phase compensation.
independentClaims: 1. An apparatus for experimental sound transduction, comprising: an acoustic input transducer configured to convert physical vibrations into an analog electrical signal; a dynamic hysteresis conditioning stage; and an acoustic output transducer configured to project conditioned sound into an architectural boundary.
2. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a real-time digital microcontroller configured to monitor spectral peaks and adjust closed-loop phase alignment.

3. A method for algorithmic spatial sound diffusion, comprising: sampling multichannel audio streams; calculating distance-based amplitude weights across distributed speaker coordinates; and routing low-latency audio packets over an asynchronous IP network.
dependentClaims: 4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the dynamic conditioning stage comprises a soft-clipping JFET transistor network.
5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the acoustic output transducer comprises an exponential horn with aluminum phase plugs.
6. The method of claim 3, wherein the network protocol is Dante operating under IEEE 1588 precision time protocol.
7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the input transducer comprises a dual-axis optical laser triangulation sensor.
